purpose: Live same-protocol macOS caller/guardian skew during an atomic binary switch
method: Build the actual previous source and use protected copies of the verified current debug pair. In each private HOME/CARGO_HOME/RGO_HOME, take the existing local session flock, start unchanged cargo run --offline, wait for RGO_TEST_SESSION_LOCK_MARKER, atomically switch the installed pair, then release the barrier. The loaded caller remains the initial binary; launchd starts the replacement guardian. Automatic GC and compiler caching remain off.
controls: Exact application stdout/stderr, one recorded application invocation, exact exit 17, real build-script OUT_DIR under the expected managed/checkout root, owned job retirement, nonempty prepared context list followed by actual idle-context deletion via rgo gc --target 0, and explicit shutdown/wait of each owned private daemon.
probe_corrections: Before any Cargo launch, the initial probe expected setup to have created the process guard file. The fixture now creates its own regular private lock file before holding it.

The first current-caller/old-guardian application returned 17 once with no commit, but its location assertion compared /private/tmp with /tmp lexically. The corrected comparison resolves both paths; only that direction was rerun to complete the remaining assertions. No rgo code was changed.
limits: This proves two healthy same-protocol nonterminal handoffs on the recorded local runtime. It does not prove installer crash/rollback, older cleanup protocols or schemas, terminal/pending-signal skew, an already-running old guardian, every runtime, or full upgrade/activation readiness. No new Rust test case or CI lane.
